Bash("C:\Program Files\GitHub CLI\gh.exe" issue create --title "[P4] Missing null checks for list element access in model_fun()" --label "enhancement" --body "$(cat <<''EOF''
## Priority: 🔵 P4 - Low

## Location
`scripts/R/functions/model_fun.R:206-207`

## Description
Direct access to nested list elements without checking if they exist or are NULL.

## Current Code
```r
os_control <- params$p_os[["control_OS"]]
pfs_control <- params$p_pfs[["control_PFS"]]
```

## Problem
- If `params$p_os` is NULL or doesn''t contain "control_OS", this fails with cryptic error
- Similar issues throughout the function for biomarker strategies
- No graceful handling of misconfigured parameter lists

## Impact
- Cryptic error messages: "subscript out of bounds" or "object of type 'NULL'"
- Difficult to diagnose when parameter lists are misconfigured
- Poor user experience when setting up new scenarios

## Recommended Fix
Add defensive checks:

```r
# Validate control survival curves exist
if (is.null(params$p_os) || is.null(params$p_os[["control_OS"]])) {
  stop("Missing control OS curve in params$p_os$control_OS")
}
if (is.null(params$p_pfs) || is.null(params$p_pfs[["control_PFS"]])) {
  stop("Missing control PFS curve in params$p_pfs$control_PFS")
}

os_control <- params$p_os[["control_OS"]]
pfs_control <- params$p_pfs[["control_PFS"]]
```

Or more concisely:
```r
os_control <- params$p_os[["control_OS"]]
pfs_control <- params$p_pfs[["control_PFS"]]
if (is.null(os_control) || is.null(pfs_control)) {
  stop("Missing control survival curves in params")
}
```

## Effort
3-5 lines per strategy (control + 3 biomarkers = ~15 lines total)
